body: I wonder if this would be better accomplished with something like #90049 rather than creating a new system for it in spinslider.

I think this is a good basis for a very non-invasive, yet attention drawing method to make users aware that certain exported properties are invalid. I have one suggestion, which is to _also_ display a warning icon inside the value field with a tooltip explaining why it is invalid and thus implying how it can be fixed. Right now it is apparent that something is wrong, but it's not immediately apparent how it can be fixed. An icon with a tooltip is one way to address that.

> I wonder if this would be better accomplished with something like #90049 rather than creating a new system for it in spinslider.

I'm not sure these issues have the same purpose. The main problem this PR attempts to address is that the Inspector displays incorrect, misleading values ​​that don't match the actual values. For example, `range_int_1` displays `10` when the actual value is `-100`. The color indication serves only to attract attention. You may notice that the correct value is displayed for enums. But previously, the Inspector misled the user by displaying the first option as selected.

#90049 has a much broader scope and is intended to display configuration warnings at the object level (including this can take into account several interrelated properties at the same time). The value of an incorrectly configured property may well have a valid value within the field constraints specified by the export hint.

Whereas this PR is intended as a _local_ indication within a property editor. That is, indication of a case where the actual value of a property for some reason is one that you cannot set in this property editor.

Can a broader warning system handle this? Yes, but in this case, it would have to account for the logic of various property editors (and the fact that a custom property editor can be used for any property). That is, it's not exactly its responsibility. This isn't a problem with the object's configuration as a whole, or even a problem with a property value not matching the export hint constraints. It's a problem with the specific implementation of a property editor, which is designed to display values ​​within a specified range, from a specified set, etc., but encounters a value that doesn't satisfy those constraints.

> I have one suggestion, which is to _also_ display a warning icon inside the value field with a tooltip explaining why it is invalid and thus implying how it can be fixed.

There's already a tooltip when hovering over a property editor. There's no error icon because it's conceptually incorrect and difficult to implement. This isn't an error with the property itself, but with the property value.

Although I find this a step in the right direction, I no longer want to continue working on it because:

1. This requires a lot of effort to check all property editors, determine which values ​​are invalid, and choose the appearance of property editors with invalid values.
2. It seems like this PR hasn't attracted much interest among maintainers or the community.

If anyone is interested in continuing to work on this, you can use this as a basis, crediting me as a co-author.
